item.title: Jensen Huang denies Trump's role in Nvidia reinstatement
item.description:
Jensen Huang denies Trump’s role in Nvidia reinstatement

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang addressed staff during his first all-hands meeting since returning to the company, explicitly denying that President Donald Trump or other political figures helped him regain his position. This update clarifies the circumstances surrounding Huang’s reinstatement following his November resignation due to personal conduct allegations.

🗣️ Huang’s Denial of Political Involvement

Huang reportedly told Nvidia staff that it is “not true” that Trump got him rehired. He dismissed claims that the President was directly involved in his reinstatement—narratives publicly promoted by Trump himself—as “completely untrue.”

  • Huang stated, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company.”
  • He also rejected the idea that his return was due to “tech bro” culture or that he was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.”
  • Huang described the surrounding narrative as the “most tortured” story in human history.

⚖️ Official Statements and Context

While Huang denied political interference, official statements from the White House suggest otherwise. The White House stated that Trump was “totally involved” in the decision to reinstate Huang.

  • Trump’s Stance: Trump confirmed working with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. In a Truth Social post, he noted the government has “no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a national security risk and that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” of “unlawful conduct.”
  • Tech Leader Support: A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, favored Huang’s return.
  • Board Decision: According to the New York Times, the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation” while receiving assurance from the government that Huang posed no national security threat.

🔍 Ongoing Investigations and Consequences

Despite his reinstatement, legal and internal scrutiny continues. Nvidia is facing an investigation regarding its accounting practices, and the company is conducting its own internal investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot.

  • Congressional Testimony: Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st regarding national security concerns. Democrats are planning to press him on his return and Trump’s involvement.
  • Personal Accountability: Huang acknowledged violating Nvidia’s code of conduct and admitted to making “terrible mistakes.” He stated, “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”
  • Current Status: Huang is attending therapy daily. He also remarked that he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.”

Source: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired

item.title: Jensen Huang Says He Is Willing to Return as Nvidia CEO
item.description:
Jensen Huang Says He Is Willing to Return as Nvidia CEO

Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week, has stated he is willing to return to the role if the company’s board of directors requests it. This statement comes after his resignation following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct report.

🔍 Background on Resignation

Huang resigned on Thursday. In a statement, he acknowledged that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.” He noted that he created problems for the Board that he deeply regrets and owns his mistakes completely. He is currently committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.

⚙️ Interim Leadership and Support

Following Huang’s departure, CFO Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO. However, significant public support for Huang’s return has emerged. More than 193,000 people, including CEOs such as Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, have signed a letter to “bring Jensen back.” President Trump has also expressed support for Huang’s return, stating that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea.”

💡 Huang’s Statement on Return

Huang said he has seen an “outpouring of calls” from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers asking him to return. He noted that many continue to reach out to him directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. He stated, “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

In the statement, Huang also reflected on his time in the U.S., noting he came to the United States 53 years ago and described becoming an American citizen as one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of his life. He emphasized that nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible.

🚀 Board Stance

Despite the public support, Nvidia’s board reportedly is “not considering” having Huang return. Nvidia did not immediately reply to a request for comment regarding this development.

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #CorporateLeadership #TechNews #CEO

Source: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO

item.title: US District Judge dismisses sexual abuse lawsuit against Sam Altman
item.description:
US District Judge dismisses sexual abuse lawsuit against Sam Altman

On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed a lawsuit filed last year by Ann Altman against her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. The lawsuit, which alleged that Sam Altman had sexually abused her throughout her childhood, was dismissed with prejudice, meaning the case cannot be refiled in that court.

⚙️ Key details

  • The dismissal occurred because Ann Altman failed to appear for an independent medical examination over the past year.
  • The plaintiff did not meet other court deadlines despite receiving warnings that failure to do so would result in the case being dismissed.
  • Judge Bluestone granted the motion to dismiss with prejudice but denied Sam Altman’s request for attorney fees and costs.

🔍 Case statements

Participant Statement or Position
Sam Altman, his mother, and his brothers Shared a statement calling the claims “deeply hurtful and entirely untrue” and stated the situation causes “immense pain” to the family.
Judge Zachary Bluestone Noted the plaintiff’s failure to appear for medical examination or meet deadlines as grounds for dismissal.
Santos Perez Ann Altman’s former lawyer stated he is “no longer authorized to comment on this case” but continues “to believe in Annie.”

#SamAltman #OpenAI #LegalNews #Litigation

Source: Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
